newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-FTSE options busy as UK shares sent higher.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-FTSE options busy as UK shares sent higher.

text.p: FTSE 100 traded options were in demand on Wednesday as FTSE futures raced up to record highs, dealers said.

One of the bigger deals was a volatility trade, which involved selling FTSE futures against a put spread. The deal was to sell 2,200 March 5025/5525 puts for a net credit of 136-1/2p against selling FTSE futures.

If FTSE futures keep going higher this will make losses from the short futures position but gains from the put spread. It may be possible to buy back the spread and establish a new put spread with higher strike prices to establish an overall profit.
Conversely, if FTSE futures weaken sufficiently then an overall loss will be made owing to a widening of the put spread by an amount greater than any gain from the short futures position.
Less complex was the deal to buy 800 October 4950 calls at prices of 186p to 190p.
There was also a buyer of 750 August 4225 calls in FTSE at 757p who hedged this by selling September futures at about 5000.
By 1435 GMT, cash FTSE was up 56.1 to 5016.7, while September futures were up 91 points to 5040.
Over in stock options there was mixed trading in British Telecommunications.
One trader bought 2,000 November 460 calls at 12p and in another trade which was executed by the same broker, 1,000 August 460 puts were bought at 65p.
BT shares slipped a penny to 416-1/2p.
